title: A response that grows
hook: Repeated events do not always have the same effect.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In this toy record, response levels after four cues are 1, 2, 3, 4. What pattern is shown?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In this toy record, response levels after four cues are 1, 2, 3, 4. What pattern is shown?

claims.text: In this toy record, response levels after four cues are 1, 2, 3, 4. What pattern is shown? The response rises from 1 to 4 across the four stipulated trials. An increasing response may be consistent with sensitization, while a decreasing response may be consistent with habituation. A single sequence does not by itself prove the underlying mechanism.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A toy response changes from 2 to 4 to 6 across three cues. Which trend is shown? Each listed value is larger than the previous one.
